note: Trigger function that keeps the new bigint column equal to customer_id on every insert/update.

In one short transaction: add nullable customer_id_new bigint (metadata only, no rewrite), a NOT VALID not-null check, and the sync trigger. The table lock is taken with a 300ms lock_timeout and retried, so app queries never queue behind it for long.
Backfill ids 1..1,000,000 in 250k-row batches, each its own transaction (the app only inserts new rows, so no row-lock conflicts).
Backfill rows above 10,000,000 that the app inserted before the trigger existed (rows inserted after it already have the value).
Verify every row: customer_id_new must equal customer_id, otherwise the plan stops here. Plain read, takes no blocking lock.
Validate the not-null check. VALIDATE takes only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, so reads and inserts keep running; once valid, SET NOT NULL can skip its table scan.

Atomic swap, metadata only, same short-lock-with-retry pattern: SET NOT NULL (proven by the valid check, no scan), drop the check and the trigger, drop the old integer column, rename customer_id_new to customer_id. The app refers to columns by name, so it needs no redeploy.
Drop the trigger function and refresh planner statistics for the new column.
Fail unless orders.customer_id is now bigint NOT NULL.
